records.Concise description: A mobile Lightning wallet that now supports both custodial and self-custodial modes depending on region and user configuration.
records.Deeper researched summary: Wallet of Satoshi historically became known for a highly simplified custodial Lightning experience. By 2026 it had introduced a self-custody model underpinned by Spark in supported markets while continuing custodial service in other contexts. The current product therefore cannot be accurately labeled simply 'custodial' or 'non-custodial' without specifying the user's mode and jurisdiction.
Creators / founders: Wallet of Satoshi / Living Room of Satoshi team
records.Launch / history: Wallet of Satoshi emerged in the late 2010s as a simple custodial Lightning wallet. Its custody architecture expanded materially with self-custody rollout using Spark by 2025–2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is a major consumer Lightning wallet and an important case study in custody-model migration: the same brand can expose materially different key-control models.
records.Verification basis: Current 2026 first-party custody disclosure verifies the coexistence of self-custodial and custodial models.
Research notes / uncertainties: This record must not receive unqualified public copy saying Wallet of Satoshi is either custodial or non-custodial; mode and region determine the answer.
Feature and availability claims are jurisdiction-sensitive and should be date-stamped in public guidance.

records.Concise description: A Bitcoin payment wallet that added a Spark-based non-custodial mode in 2026 while continuing or winding down custodial service depending on region.
records.Deeper researched summary: Blink evolved from the Bitcoin Beach / Galoy wallet lineage and historically used a custodial account model optimized for circular-economy payments. In June 2026 Blink launched a non-custodial Spark mode with user-controlled recovery. Its terms distinguish Custodial Mode from Non-Custodial Mode, and 2026 regional changes included winding down some hosted/custodial services. The canonical profile therefore preserves both modes instead of forcing one custody label.
Creators / founders: Nicolas Burtey — Galoy co-founder / public project lead
records.Launch / history: Originated from the Bitcoin Beach Wallet/Galoy ecosystem and rebranded to Blink in 2023. Non-custodial Spark mode launched June 24, 2026, followed by regional custodial-service changes in mid-2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: Blink is important for Bitcoin payment adoption and for its explicit transition from a primarily custodial community wallet toward a mixed architecture with user-controlled Spark balances.
records.Verification basis: Current June–August 2026 first-party announcements and terms verify Spark non-custody, the continuing distinction between custody modes and regional service changes.
Research notes / uncertainties: This record should not receive unqualified 'self-custody' or 'custodial' copy; the answer depends on wallet mode and region.
Regional hosted-service wind-downs are time-sensitive and should be rechecked before publication.

records.Concise description: Bull Bitcoin's open-source Bitcoin-only self-custody mobile wallet combining on-chain BTC, Liquid and swap-based Lightning payments with PayJoin and hardware-wallet ambitions.
records.Deeper researched summary: Bull Bitcoin Wallet is a Bitcoin-only mobile wallet that keeps user keys under self-custody while supporting separate Bitcoin and Liquid balances and automatic cross-network routing. Lightning payments are handled through swaps rather than a user-managed Lightning channel balance. The wallet also supports PayJoin and is developing broad hardware-wallet companion functionality.
Creators / founders: Francis Pouliot — founder / CEO of Bull Bitcoin
records.Launch / history: Developed by the long-running Bull Bitcoin company and released as a standalone Bitcoin wallet in the mid-2020s; active development continued through 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It combines Bitcoin-only product philosophy with practical on-chain, Liquid and Lightning payment interoperability and includes PayJoin as a first-class privacy tool.
records.Verification basis: Current Bull Bitcoin first-party wallet/product material verifies self-custody, Bitcoin-only scope, payment rails, PayJoin and hardware-wallet direction.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not describe Bull Bitcoin Wallet as a native Lightning-node wallet; Lightning payments use swap-based interoperability.
Exchange/on-ramp services from Bull Bitcoin are separate from custody of keys in the wallet.

records.Entity / project type: multisig Bitcoin wallet / assisted self-custody platform
records.Concise description: A Bitcoin-focused multisig wallet and coordination platform with hardware-key support, assisted recovery and inheritance tooling.
records.Deeper researched summary: Nunchuk is a self-custody Bitcoin wallet built around multi-key policies. Users can construct ordinary multisig setups with software and hardware keys or use assisted services where Nunchuk holds a minority platform key that cannot spend unilaterally. Current products include inheritance designs using timelocks and dedicated beneficiary/inheritance keys, and experimental Taproot/MuSig2 multisig functionality.
records.Launch / history: Nunchuk launched around 2020 and has expanded from a multisig coordinator into assisted multisig, inheritance and collaborative key-management services. New inheritance features continued shipping in 2026.
records.Why it matters in the Bitcoin wallet eco: It is one of the clearest Bitcoin-native examples of separating key coordination and recovery assistance from unilateral custody.
Important technical or cultural characte: Assisted multisig with minority platform key
Taproot / MuSig2 multisig remains an explicitly experimental/beta area in source material
records.Verification basis: Current Nunchuk platform and 2026 inheritance documentation verify active operation, multisig architecture and the limited role of Nunchuk-held keys.
Research notes / uncertainties: Do not call assisted Nunchuk plans 'custodial' merely because Nunchuk may hold one key; verify whether Nunchuk has a spending quorum in the specific plan.
Taproot/MuSig2 features have been described as beta/experimental; do not present them as the default safety baseline without a fresh publication check.
